Moving early childhood policy forward: “3 speed up, 3 reduce, 3 increase” and less screen time for young children
se: The meeting considered how to move early childhood policy forward to support children's development in times of crisis. A working group of the Office of the Education Council (OEC) presented the policy proposal “3 speed up, 3 reduce, 3 increase”, which the Cabinet has already approved. The 3 speed-ups are: give parents knowledge, promote universal child welfare, and strengthen local government organisations. The 3 reductions are: less screen use, less stress and less violence. The 3 increases are: more development activities through housework, gardening and cooking, more use of storybooks, and more quality family time. The OEC and its partners have declared an intention of no screens for children under 2, made media and radio and television programmes, and held meetings to build understanding in Chiang Mai, Nakhon Ratchasima and Phuket. The plan for 2027 extends the work to reducing violence together with reducing screen time, promotes music, art and sport, and reaches village health volunteers and civil society. The meeting suggested that early childhood is the most important foundation of national development and that knowledge and practical guidance should reach front-line workers, such as teachers, school leaders, child carers under local government, village health volunteers and parents. The subcommittee chair suggested that the OEC study ways to control the use of smartphones and tablets in schools for young and school-age children.
it: Policy proposal “3 speed up, 3 reduce, 3 increase” for early childhood development in times of crisis, results so far and plan for 2027 (OEC)
Suggestions: get knowledge to front-line workers, and study ways to control smartphone and tablet use in schools

Starting a study on the Learning Promotion Act, and approving the report on children without Thai nationality
se: The meeting considered 2 matters. First, the plan to study and make policy proposals on the results of the Learning Promotion Act B.E. 2023 and the effectiveness of the Department of Learning Encouragement. The study covers 5 points: the number of graduates compared with the number of learners, the clarity of indicators and databases, the issuing of secondary legislation, how well the budget matches the plan, and care for vulnerable groups together with other agencies, such as out-of-school children, persons with disabilities and older persons. The study is expected to take about 6 months. The meeting approved the project, its objectives, scope and work plan, and asked for coordination with other subcommittees to avoid duplicate studies. Second, a review of the study report on education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers (Myanmar) in Samut Sakhon and Tak. Its substance is unchanged, but its data was updated and its format adjusted to the handbook of the Office of the Secretary-General of the Senate. The meeting approved the report and sent it to the committee, to be put to the Senate under rules 98 and 99.
it: Study project on the results of the Learning Promotion Act B.E. 2023 and the effectiveness of the Department of Learning Encouragement (about 6 months)
Study report on education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers (Myanmar) in Samut Sakhon and Tak (revised)
